artworks.title: Improvisation No. 30 (Cannons)
artworks.description: Swirling lines and bursts of colour fill the canvas. In the lower right, two cannons can be made out among the shapes, a rare hint of a real subject in Kandinsky’s early abstract work.

artworks.title: Painting with Green Center
artworks.description: A green shape sits at the centre of a crowded, energetic composition of colour and line. The painting shows Kandinsky moving away from recognisable subjects altogether.

artworks.title: Composition (No. 1) Gray-Red
artworks.description: Black lines divide a pale surface into rectangles, with a single block of red. Mondrian used only straight lines and a few colours to create balance.

artworks.title: Landscape with Two Poplars
artworks.description: Two tall poplar trees still anchor this landscape, but the hills, sky and figures are dissolving into bright, free patches of colour.

artworks.title: Composition VII
artworks.description: Kandinsky’s most complex pre-war painting: a storm of colour, line and shape with no single centre. He made more than thirty studies before painting it in a few days.

artworks.title: Composition VIII
artworks.description: Painted during his Bauhaus years, it swaps the stormy forms of his earlier work for circles, triangles and crisp lines balanced on a calm, pale ground.
artworks.collection: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York

artworks.title: Edtaonisl (Ecclesiastic)
artworks.description: Inspired by a dancer and a priest Picabia watched on an ocean voyage, the figures break apart into a rhythm of flat, interlocking planes of colour.

artworks.title: Champs de Mars: The Red Tower
artworks.description: The Eiffel Tower seems to sway and shatter among fragments of Paris, as Delaunay paints the energy of the modern city seen from many angles at once.

artworks.title: Black Square
artworks.description: A single black square on white: Malevich called it the “zero of form”, a starting point for painting made of pure shape and feeling. Age has cracked the black paint.

artworks.title: Water Lily Pond
artworks.description: Monet painted the Japanese footbridge over the water-lily pond in his garden at Giverny many times. Here the bridge, foliage and lilies melt into soft strokes of green, violet and rose.

artworks.title: Cliff Walk at Pourville
artworks.description: Two figures stand on a windy clifftop above the sea on the Normandy coast. Quick, broken brushstrokes capture moving grass, light and air.

artworks.title: Auvers, Panoramic View
artworks.description: A view over the rooftops of a French village, built up from blocks of colour. Cezanne’s careful structure points towards later modern painting.

artworks.title: View of Genoa
artworks.medium: Oil on paper, mounted on canvas
artworks.description: A bright, quiet view of the Italian port city of Genoa, painted outdoors. Corot’s clear light and simple shapes influenced the Impressionists.

artworks.title: Landscape, Sunset
artworks.description: Warm evening light glows behind soft, dark trees. Inness used hazy tones to create a peaceful, almost dreamlike mood.

artworks.title: Valley of Aosta: Snowstorm, Avalanche, and Thunderstorm
artworks.description: A storm, an avalanche and a thunderstorm sweep through an Alpine valley. Turner turns the power of nature into whirling light and colour.

artworks.title: Stacks of Wheat (End of Summer)
artworks.description: Part of Monet’s famous series painted near his home at Giverny, studying the same stacks of wheat in changing light, season and weather.

artworks.title: Starry Night Over the Rhône
artworks.description: Gas lamps and stars shimmer on the river at Arles while a couple strolls along the bank — painted outdoors at night, a year before The Starry Night.

artworks.title: Wheat Field with Cypresses
artworks.description: Golden wheat, a dark flame-like cypress and swirling clouds — one of the summer landscapes Van Gogh painted near the asylum at Saint-Rémy.

artworks.title: Impression, Sunrise
artworks.description: The harbour of Le Havre in morning mist, with an orange sun reflected in the water. A critic mocked its title, and the name “Impressionism” was born.

artworks.title: The Hay Wain
artworks.description: A horse-drawn cart crosses the River Stour in Suffolk under a bright, cloud-filled sky — one of the best-loved images of the English countryside.

artworks.title: Still Life with Flowers
artworks.description: A loose bouquet seems to float against a soft, glowing background. Redon’s flowers feel more like a dream than a careful record.

artworks.title: Bouquet of Flowers in an Earthenware Vase
artworks.description: Dozens of flowers, many blooming at different times of year, are gathered into one impossible bouquet against a dark background.

artworks.title: Chrysanthemums
artworks.description: A full vase of chrysanthemums painted with soft, feathery strokes of warm colour.

artworks.title: Magnolias on Light Blue Velvet Cloth
artworks.description: Large white magnolia blossoms lie on a soft blue cloth, painted with smooth, careful detail.

artworks.title: Roses in a Bowl
artworks.description: Soft pink and white roses spill over a simple bowl against a dark, plain background, painted with the quiet realism Fantin-Latour was famous for.

artworks.title: Sunflowers
artworks.description: Van Gogh’s repetition of his famous Arles still life, painting yellow on yellow to show the sunflowers from full bloom to wilting.

artworks.title: Irises
artworks.description: Painted in the garden of the asylum at Saint-Rémy in his first week there; a single white iris stands out among a crowd of blue.
artworks.collection: J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles

artworks.title: Flowers in a Glass Vase
artworks.description: Roses, tulips and lilies glow against a dark background in this carefully arranged bouquet by one of the most celebrated Dutch flower painters.

artworks.title: Bouquet of Flowers in an Urn
artworks.description: A tumbling bouquet of flowers from every season, with tiny insects hidden among the petals — painted with the fine detail Van Huysum was famous for.
artworks.collection: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

artworks.title: Bouquet of Sunflowers
artworks.description: Monet’s loose, lively brushwork turns a vase of sunflowers on a red tablecloth into a burst of colour — painted seven years before Van Gogh’s famous versions.
artworks.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

artworks.title: View of Cotopaxi
artworks.description: The Cotopaxi volcano in Ecuador rises above a lush tropical valley. Church travelled to South America to paint its scenery.

artworks.title: The Home of the Heron
artworks.description: A lone heron stands in a misty marsh at dusk. Soft golden light and dark trees create a quiet, thoughtful mood.

artworks.title: Distant View of Niagara Falls
artworks.description: Niagara Falls appears in the distance beyond wild trees and rocks, as it might have looked before towns grew up around it.

artworks.title: Pond in the Woods
artworks.artist: Narcisse Virgile Diaz de la Peña
artworks.description: Light breaks through the trees onto a still pond deep in the forest. Barbizon painters loved working outdoors in the woods near Paris.

artworks.title: Mist Rising at Sunset in the Catskills
artworks.description: Golden mist fills a mountain valley at sunset. Gifford was known for paintings full of glowing, hazy light.

artworks.title: The Herring Net
artworks.description: Two fishermen haul a heavy net full of herring into their small boat on a rough grey sea.

artworks.title: Among the Sierra Nevada, California
artworks.description: Painted in Rome from sketches made in the American West: a sunlit lake, waterfalls and storm clouds make the Sierra Nevada look like an untouched paradise.
artworks.collection: Smithsonian American Art Museum, Washington, D.C.

artworks.title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
artworks.description: A lone figure stands on a rocky peak, his back to us, looking out over a sea of mist — an icon of Romantic awe before nature.

artworks.title: The Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone
artworks.description: Moran’s huge canvas of the canyon’s glowing cliffs and falling river helped persuade the U.S. Congress to protect Yellowstone as the first national park.
artworks.collection: Smithsonian American Art Museum, Washington, D.C.

artworks.title: Twilight in the Wilderness
artworks.description: A blazing red and gold sunset over an untouched forest and river, painted on the eve of the American Civil War.

artworks.title: The Fighting Temeraire
artworks.description: A ghostly old warship is towed to be broken up by a small black steam tug under a fiery sunset — Turner’s farewell to the age of sail.

artworks.title: Two Sisters (On the Terrace)
artworks.description: A young woman and a little girl sit on a terrace above the river, surrounded by flowers and greenery.

artworks.title: The Child’s Bath
artworks.description: A woman gently washes a child’s feet. Seen from above, the scene feels close and tender.

artworks.title: Oil Sketch for “A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884”
artworks.description: A small study for Seurat’s famous painting of Parisians relaxing on an island in the River Seine, made with short dabs of colour.

artworks.title: Interrupted Reading
artworks.medium: Oil on canvas, mounted on board
artworks.description: A young woman rests her head on her hand, a book open on her lap, lost in thought.

artworks.title: On a Balcony
artworks.description: A woman in a pale dress reads a newspaper on a balcony full of plants and soft daylight.

artworks.title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
artworks.description: A girl in a blue and yellow turban turns to look over her shoulder, a large pearl catching the light — a study of a face rather than a portrait of a known sitter.

artworks.title: Paris Street; Rainy Day
artworks.description: Elegant Parisians with umbrellas cross a wet, newly built boulevard; Caillebotte’s crisp detail and wide view capture modern city life.

artworks.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884
artworks.description: Seurat’s masterpiece: Parisians relax by the Seine, painted in tiny dots of pure colour that blend in the viewer’s eye. It took him two years.

artworks.title: Luncheon of the Boating Party
artworks.description: Renoir’s friends share lunch on a restaurant balcony by the Seine, in a joyful scene full of light, conversation and flirtation.

artworks.title: Self-Portrait
artworks.description: Painted in Paris, where Van Gogh discovered Impressionism and Seurat’s dots — his face is built from short, rhythmic strokes of bright colour.

artworks.title: Virgin and Child with Two Angels
artworks.description: Mary holds the infant Christ, with two angels beside them, in a round painting from Renaissance Florence.

artworks.title: The Annunciation
artworks.description: A bible story set in a sunlit field of white lilies, painted by an American artist working in the Netherlands.

artworks.title: Saint Martin and the Beggar
artworks.description: Saint Martin, on a white horse, cuts his cloak in half to share it with a beggar. El Greco stretches the figures to make them feel spiritual.

artworks.title: The Crucifixion
artworks.description: A gold-background panel from the Italian Renaissance, painted with sharp detail and rich colour.

artworks.title: The Adoration of the Magi
artworks.description: The three kings bring gifts to the infant Christ, surrounded by a crowd of richly dressed followers.

artworks.title: Annunciation
artworks.description: An early work by Leonardo: the angel Gabriel kneels before Mary in a walled garden, with a misty landscape opening up behind them.

artworks.title: Sistine Madonna
artworks.description: Mary steps forward on the clouds holding the Christ Child, between Pope Sixtus II and Saint Barbara; the two cherubs below became famous on their own.

artworks.title: The Assumption of the Virgin
artworks.description: El Greco’s first major commission in Spain: the apostles gather around Mary’s empty tomb as she rises into heaven surrounded by angels.

artworks.title: The Calling of Saint Matthew
artworks.description: A beam of light follows Christ’s pointing hand into a dim tax office, where Matthew is called to become a disciple — a landmark of dramatic Baroque lighting.
